questions.explanation: A = 6000 + 4(1200) = RM10800; B = 2000 + 6(1200) = RM9200. Dengan kekangan lain setara, B lebih murah sebanyak RM1600.

note.title: Pelarasan akruan dan kualiti untung
note.summary: Membezakan aliran tunai, hasil diperoleh dan belanja bagi tempoh.
body: Asas akruan mengaitkan hasil dan belanja dengan tempoh yang relevan, bukan semata-mata masa wang diterima atau dibayar. Hasil diterima terdahulu belum menjadi hasil diperoleh jika perkhidmatan masih belum diberikan. Belanja terakru pula diiktiraf apabila berkaitan dengan tempoh semasa walaupun bayarannya akan dibuat kemudian.

Contoh kerja: akaun belum laras merekod semua premium insurans RM2400 sebagai belanja pada 1 Oktober untuk perlindungan dua belas bulan. Pada 31 Disember, tiga bulan telah digunakan: belanja ialah RM600 dan insurans prabayar RM1800. Pelarasan mendebit aset prabayar dan mengkredit belanja sebanyak RM1800, lalu meningkatkan untung berbanding angka belum laras.

Salah tanggapan ialah menganggap pelarasan ini menambah tunai. Tunai telah dibayar pada Oktober; pelarasan mengubah pengelasan serta masa pengiktirafan. Semasa menyelesaikan soalan, kenal pasti catatan awal, tempoh digunakan dan baki masa depan sebelum menentukan kesan terhadap untung, aset atau liabiliti.
keyPoints: Bezakan wang diterima daripada hasil yang telah diperoleh.
Tentukan catatan awal sebelum menulis jurnal pelarasan.
Pelarasan bukan tunai boleh mengubah untung dan kedudukan kewangan.

reading.title: Pusat latihan dan yuran awal
reading.summary: Menganalisis mengapa tunai yang tinggi belum membuktikan untung tinggi.
body: Pusat latihan rekaan menerima RM18000 pada Disember untuk kursus yang akan diadakan sepenuhnya pada Januari. Kerani merekod semua penerimaan itu sebagai hasil Disember. Pada bulan yang sama, pusat belum membayar RM2400 gaji tutor bagi kelas Disember dan belanja itu belum direkodkan. Pemilik menganggap baki bank yang meningkat membuktikan prestasi bulanan sangat baik. Akauntan meminta jadual kursus dan rekod kerja tutor sebelum menutup akaun. Dia menjelaskan bahawa perkhidmatan Januari masih menjadi tanggungjawab pusat, manakala kerja tutor Disember telah digunakan. Maklumat tentang aliran tunai tetap penting, tetapi ia menjawab persoalan yang berbeza daripada pengukuran untung tempoh tersebut.

questions.prompt: Apakah pelarasan bagi RM18000 yang telah direkod sebagai hasil Disember?
options: Debit tunai RM18000; kredit modal RM18000
Debit belanja RM18000; kredit tunai RM18000
Debit hasil diterima terdahulu RM18000; kredit hasil RM18000
Debit hasil RM18000; kredit hasil diterima terdahulu RM18000
questions.hint: Perkhidmatan belum diberi, jadi pindahkan hasil belum diperoleh kepada liabiliti.
questions.explanation: Pelarasan membatalkan pengiktirafan hasil Disember dan mengiktiraf obligasi perkhidmatan masa depan. Tunai tidak dicatat sekali lagi kerana sudah diterima.

questions.prompt: Berapakah jumlah penurunan untung Disember daripada kedua-dua pelarasan?
questions.hint: Hasil berkurang dan belanja gaji bertambah.
questions.explanation: Pengurangan hasil RM18000 serta tambahan belanja RM2400 kedua-duanya menurunkan untung. Jumlah kesan ialah RM20400, bukan perbezaan antara dua angka itu.

practice.title: Menutup akaun Firma Seroja rekaan
practice.summary: Mengira untung laras serta aset dan liabiliti daripada maklumat lengkap.
body: Pada 31 Disember, untung belum laras ialah RM42000. Insurans RM3600 dibayar pada 1 Oktober untuk 12 bulan dan seluruhnya direkod sebagai belanja. Gaji Disember RM1500 belum dibayar atau direkod. Peralatan berharga RM24000, tersedia digunakan sejak 1 Januari, mempunyai nilai baki sifar dan hayat guna empat tahun; susut nilai garis lurus tahun ini belum direkod. Tiada pelarasan lain dan tiada cukai dalam model ini.

questions.prompt: Berapakah insurans prabayar pada 31 Disember?
options: RM900
RM300
questions.hint: Sembilan daripada dua belas bulan perlindungan belum digunakan.
questions.explanation: RM3600 × 9/12 = RM2700. Tiga bulan yang digunakan berjumlah RM900; kerana semua bayaran dicatat sebagai belanja, RM2700 perlu dipindahkan kepada aset.

questions.prompt: Apakah jurnal pelarasan bagi gaji?
options: Debit belanja gaji RM1500; kredit gaji terakru RM1500
Debit gaji terakru RM1500; kredit tunai RM1500
Debit tunai RM1500; kredit hasil RM1500
Debit peralatan RM1500; kredit belanja gaji RM1500
questions.hint: Kerja telah digunakan tetapi bayaran masih terhutang.
questions.explanation: Belanja bertambah melalui debit dan liabiliti gaji terakru bertambah melalui kredit. Tunai belum bergerak pada tarikh pelarasan.

questions.prompt: Berapakah susut nilai tahunan peralatan?
questions.hint: Agihkan amaun boleh disusut nilai kepada empat tahun.
questions.explanation: (RM24000 − RM0) ÷ 4 = RM6000. Peralatan tersedia sepanjang tahun, jadi tiada pelarasan sebahagian tahun diperlukan.

questions.prompt: Berapakah untung selepas semua pelarasan?
questions.hint: Mulakan RM42000, pulangkan belanja prabayar dan tolak dua belanja tambahan.
questions.explanation: RM42000 + RM2700 − RM1500 − RM6000 = RM37200. Pelarasan insurans meningkatkan untung kerana belanja awal terlebih rekod, sementara gaji dan susut nilai menurunkannya.

note.title: Foundations: linear programming with two variables
note.summary: A preparatory two-variable model; this unit does not cover the full STPM simplex and Big-M requirements.
body: This is a foundation unit for understanding variables, constraints and an objective before advanced linear programming. It uses two variables and a graphical vertex method. The revised STPM Management Mathematics syllabus develops three-variable models, simplex tableaux and the Big-M method in Semester 3. Those methods are not taught or assessed in this unit; completing it does not establish mastery of that semester topic.

A linear programming model distinguishes decision variables, an objective function and constraints. A feasible solution satisfies every constraint, including non-negativity. For a bounded polygonal feasible region, a linear objective attains an optimum at a vertex; an entire edge can also be optimal when the objective is parallel to that edge. Feasibility must be checked before comparing profits.

Worked example: maximise Z = 30x + 20y subject to x + y ≤ 8, 2x + y ≤ 12 and x, y ≥ 0. The vertices are (0,0), (0,8), (4,4) and (6,0). Their objective values are 0, 160, 200 and 180, so (4,4) is optimal with Z = 200.

A common misconception selects the product with the highest profit per unit and ignores resource use. Another assumes both resources must always be exhausted. Binding constraints describe this particular optimum; changing profits or available resources can change which constraints bind and which production mix is best.
keyPoints: Define variables and units before forming inequalities.
Check every constraint before evaluating an objective.
An optimum and its binding constraints depend on the model assumptions.

reading.title: Planning workshop time
reading.summary: An original model distinguishes a profitable idea from a feasible plan.
body: A workshop makes two divisible batches of learning kits, x and y. Every batch uses one hour of finishing time, and only ten hours are available. A separate specialist process limits x to six batches. Contributions are RM5 per batch of x and RM3 per batch of y, with no other constraints apart from non-negativity. The supervisor suggests producing ten batches of x because it has the larger contribution. The planner instead draws the feasible region and evaluates its vertices. She records that contributions are assumed constant, unused time has no alternative value in this model, and fractions of a batch are permitted.

questions.prompt: Why is the supervisor’s proposed plan infeasible?
options: It uses fewer than ten finishing hours
It exceeds the specialist limit x ≤ 6
Its contribution must be negative
Non-negativity requires x to be zero
questions.hint: Check the specialist constraint separately from total finishing time.
questions.explanation: Ten batches of x satisfy the finishing limit but violate x ≤ 6. A plan must satisfy all constraints, not just the total time restriction.

questions.prompt: Which feasible plan maximises contribution?
options: x = 0, y = 10, giving RM30
x = 5, y = 5, giving RM40
x = 6, y = 0, giving RM30
x = 6, y = 4, giving RM42
questions.hint: Use as much higher-contribution x as permitted, then check remaining time.
questions.explanation: With identical finishing use, x is preferred until its limit of six. The remaining four hours support y, producing 5(6) + 3(4) = RM42; this also agrees with the vertex comparison.

practice.title: Two resources in a production model
practice.summary: Solve a constrained optimum and a small capacity change.
body: Maximise contribution Z = 40x + 50y, in RM, subject to x + 2y ≤ 16, 3x + y ≤ 18 and x, y ≥ 0. Variables represent divisible batches. Both constraints express resource limits, and there are no other costs or restrictions. For the resource-increase case only, increase the first limit from 16 to 17 while leaving the second limit and objective unchanged.

questions.prompt: Which of the following points is feasible?
questions.hint: Substitute each pair into both resource inequalities.
questions.explanation: At (2,5), x + 2y = 12 ≤ 16 and 3x + y = 11 ≤ 18. Each other point exceeds at least one resource limit.

questions.prompt: Where do the two original resource boundaries intersect?
questions.hint: Solve x + 2y = 16 and 3x + y = 18 simultaneously.
questions.explanation: From x = 16 − 2y, substitution gives 48 − 5y = 18, hence y = 6 and x = 4. Both boundaries are exactly met.

questions.prompt: What is the original maximum contribution?
options: RM400
RM240
RM500
RM460
questions.hint: Compare the intersection with feasible axis vertices.
questions.explanation: Vertices are (0,0), (0,8), (4,6) and (6,0), giving 0, 400, 460 and 240. The maximum is RM460 at (4,6).

questions.prompt: After the first limit rises to 17, what is the new maximum?
options: RM460 at the unchanged point only
questions.hint: Recompute the intersection, then compare the new axis vertices.
questions.explanation: Solving x + 2y = 17 and 3x + y = 18 gives x = 3.8, y = 6.6 and Z = 482. New axis values are 425 and 240, so the intersection remains optimal; the gain is RM22.

note.title: Stationary points and accumulated area
note.summary: Connect derivative signs, local extrema and definite integrals.
body: Differentiation describes local change, while integration accumulates signed contributions across an interval. Solving f′(x) = 0 identifies stationary candidates, but classification requires more evidence. A change from positive to negative derivative gives a local maximum; a change from negative to positive gives a local minimum. A stationary point need not be either.

Worked example: g(x) = x³ − 3x has derivative 3(x − 1)(x + 1). The derivative is positive outside −1 < x < 1 and negative inside, so x = −1 is a local maximum and x = 1 a local minimum. Their values are 2 and −2 respectively.

A common misconception equates every definite integral with geometric area. If a graph crosses its baseline, signed contributions can cancel. Find crossings and examine signs before calculating area; for an absolute maximum on a closed interval, also compare endpoint values with the stationary candidates.
keyPoints: Use derivative signs or a valid second-derivative test to classify candidates.
Compare endpoints when an absolute extremum on a closed interval is required.
Geometric area requires non-negative contributions relative to the baseline.

reading.title: A model of a changing signal
reading.summary: An original laboratory account separates rate, level and accumulated effect.
body: A student models a dimensionless signal by h(t) = t³ − 3t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3. She calculates h′(t) = 3t(t − 2) and notices that the derivative vanishes at t = 2. A partner calls this point a maximum because the signal has stopped decreasing there. They examine values on either side: the derivative is negative between zero and two, then positive between two and three. They also note that h(0) and h(3) are both zero. Before reporting a total geometric area between the graph and the time axis, they discuss whether the integral’s sign should be retained.

questions.prompt: How should the stationary point at t = 2 be classified?
options: A local maximum, because the derivative is zero
A point where the signal is necessarily zero
A local minimum, because the derivative changes from negative to positive
A discontinuity, because a derivative changes sign
questions.hint: Track the direction of change immediately before and after two.
questions.explanation: The signal decreases before t = 2 and increases afterwards. Its value there is −4; a zero derivative does not by itself imply either a maximum or a zero signal.

questions.prompt: What is the geometric area between h and the axis over [0,3]?
options: 27/4 square units
−27/4 square units
0 square units
9/2 square units
questions.hint: Factor h(t) = t²(t − 3) to determine its sign.
questions.explanation: The graph is non-positive on [0,3]. Its integral is [t⁴/4 − t³]₀³ = −27/4, so geometric area is the positive value 27/4.

practice.title: Analyse a cubic on a closed interval
practice.summary: Use one complete function to connect algebra, extrema and area.
body: Let f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 2 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. The baseline used in the final area question is y = 2, and that question concerns only 0 ≤ x ≤ 3. All quantities are dimensionless. Distinguish local extrema from the largest value over the entire stated interval.

questions.prompt: What are the stationary x-values?
options: x = 0 and x = 3
x = 2 only
x = −1 and x = −3
x = 1 and x = 3
questions.hint: Differentiate and factor the resulting quadratic.
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 3x² − 12x + 9 = 3(x − 1)(x − 3), so the two stationary values are 1 and 3.

questions.prompt: Which classification is correct?
options: Local minima at both x = 1 and x = 3
A local maximum at x = 1 and a local minimum at x = 3
A local minimum at x = 1 and a local maximum at x = 3
Neither point can be classified because f′ is zero
questions.hint: Use f″(x) = 6x − 12 or the signs of f′.
questions.explanation: f″(1) = −6 identifies a local maximum and f″(3) = 6 a local minimum. Equivalently, derivative signs change + to − and then − to +.

questions.prompt: Where is the absolute maximum on [0,4] attained?
options: Only at x = 1, with value 6
Only at x = 3, with value 2
At both x = 1 and x = 4, with value 6
At x = 0, with value 9
questions.hint: Evaluate both endpoints as well as stationary points.
questions.explanation: f(0) = 2, f(1) = 6, f(3) = 2 and f(4) = 6. The largest value is attained at the interior local maximum and the right endpoint.

questions.prompt: What is the area between f(x) and y = 2 from x = 0 to x = 3?
options: 51/4 square units
27/4 square units
9 square units
−27/4 square units
questions.hint: Integrate f(x) − 2 after noting it equals x(x − 3)².
questions.explanation: The difference is non-negative on [0,3]. Its integral is [x⁴/4 − 2x³ + 9x²/2]₀³ = 81/4 − 54 + 81/2 = 27/4. Integrating f alone would include the rectangle below the baseline.

note.title: Functional dependencies and update anomalies
note.summary: Design relational tables using stated business rules and stable keys.
body: A functional dependency X → Y means that each permitted value of X determines one value of Y under the system’s business rules. It is a constraint on all valid states, not a coincidence in a small sample. Normalisation uses dependencies to reduce avoidable repetition and the insertion, update or deletion anomalies it can create.

Worked example: an enrolment table has StudentID, ModuleID, StudentName and Grade, with key (StudentID, ModuleID). StudentID determines StudentName, while the full key determines Grade. Repeating the name in every enrolment creates a partial dependency. Separate Student(StudentID, StudentName) from Enrolment(StudentID, ModuleID, Grade), then link records through StudentID.

A common misconception says adding an arbitrary ID automatically fixes normalisation. A surrogate key can identify rows while the original dependencies and duplicated facts remain. Another assumes normalisation alone guarantees correctness: keys, foreign keys and validation rules are still needed to enforce permitted relationships and values.
keyPoints: Derive dependencies from business rules rather than accidental sample patterns.
Store a fact with the key on which it depends.
Use integrity constraints alongside decomposition.

reading.title: An equipment checkout register
reading.summary: An original case exposes a repeated fact and an update anomaly.
body: A college register stores CheckoutID, DeviceID, DeviceModel, BorrowerID and ReturnDate in every row. Each device has one fixed model, but a device may be checked out many times. During data entry, staff correct the model name for one checkout while older rows retain the previous spelling. A report now lists two models for the same DeviceID. The technician proposes a Device table with one row per DeviceID, leaving DeviceID as a reference in each checkout. Staff also require a rule that prevents a checkout from referring to a device absent from the Device table. They want the design to preserve complete checkout history.

questions.prompt: Which dependency explains the repeated model fact?
options: DeviceID → DeviceModel
ReturnDate → BorrowerID
DeviceModel → CheckoutID
BorrowerID → DeviceID
questions.hint: Use the rule about one fixed model for each device.
questions.explanation: A DeviceID determines its model across all checkouts. Return dates and borrowers do not determine unique checkout or device identities under the stated rules.

questions.prompt: What constraint directly prevents references to nonexistent devices?
options: A larger font for DeviceModel
A rule that sorts checkouts by ReturnDate
A comment asking staff to remember every device
A foreign key from Checkout.DeviceID to Device.DeviceID
questions.hint: Choose an enforced relationship between the two tables.
questions.explanation: A foreign key checks that the referenced device exists. Sorting and presentation changes do not enforce referential integrity.

practice.title: Decomposing a project allocation table
practice.summary: Identify partial and transitive dependencies from explicit rules.
body: Allocation(EmployeeID, ProjectID, EmployeeName, DepartmentID, DepartmentName, Hours) has composite key (EmployeeID, ProjectID). Each employee belongs to one department. Rules: EmployeeID → EmployeeName, DepartmentID; DepartmentID → DepartmentName; (EmployeeID, ProjectID) → Hours. A department can contain many employees, and a project can contain many employees. No other functional dependencies are assumed. All stored values are atomic.

questions.prompt: Which fact depends on the whole composite key under these rules?
options: EmployeeName
Hours
DepartmentName
DepartmentID
questions.hint: Find the dependency whose determinant uses both identifiers.
questions.explanation: The allocated hours belong to one employee–project pair. Employee and department details can be determined without ProjectID, so they do not depend on the whole composite key.

questions.prompt: Why is EmployeeName a partial dependency in the original table?
options: EmployeeName has fewer letters than DepartmentName
EmployeeName must contain several values in one cell
ProjectID alone determines every employee name
EmployeeID alone, a proper part of the composite key, determines it
questions.hint: Partial dependency concerns the determinant, not the length of a field.
questions.explanation: The whole key is (EmployeeID, ProjectID), but EmployeeID alone determines EmployeeName. This causes the same employee fact to repeat across project allocations.

questions.prompt: After separating Employee(EmployeeID, EmployeeName, DepartmentID, DepartmentName), what remains to be addressed?
options: DepartmentName depends transitively on EmployeeID through DepartmentID
Hours has become the primary key of Employee
ProjectID now determines all department names
EmployeeName must be split into one table per character
questions.hint: Follow EmployeeID → DepartmentID → DepartmentName.
questions.explanation: DepartmentName is a department fact repeated among its employees. A separate Department(DepartmentID, DepartmentName) removes that transitive repetition while Employee retains DepartmentID.

questions.prompt: Which decomposition best matches the stated dependencies?
options: Employee(EmployeeID, Hours), Department(DepartmentID, ProjectID), Allocation(EmployeeName, DepartmentName)
One table containing only a new AllocationID plus every original repeated field
Employee(EmployeeID, EmployeeName, DepartmentID), Department(DepartmentID, DepartmentName), Allocation(EmployeeID, ProjectID, Hours)
One table per project with employee and department names copied into every row
questions.hint: Place employee, department and allocation facts with their respective keys.
questions.explanation: The three tables place each fact with its determinant and retain identifiers needed for joins. Appropriate primary and foreign keys then enforce identity and references; merely adding an ID would leave repeated facts unchanged.

note.title: Magnetic flux and induced emf
note.summary: Track area orientation, flux linkage and the direction of change.
body: Magnetic flux through a flat loop in a uniform field is Φ = BA cos θ, where θ is measured between the field and the normal to the loop’s plane. For N identical turns, flux linkage is NΦ. Faraday’s law gives induced emf as −d(NΦ)/dt; its magnitude depends on how quickly linkage changes, rather than simply how large the field is.
Worked example: a 50-turn coil has area 0.020 m² with its normal parallel to the field. If B increases uniformly from 0.10 T to 0.30 T in 0.40 s, the emf magnitude is 50 × 0.020 × 0.20/0.40 = 0.50 V.

A common misconception measures θ from the coil’s plane and uses the same cosine expression. Another treats the minus sign as a negative magnitude. Lenz’s law instead describes a direction opposing the change in flux. Induced current also requires a closed conducting path; an emf can exist across an open coil.
keyPoints: Measure θ from the area normal when using BA cos θ.
Distinguish flux per turn from total flux linkage.
Use the change in flux to determine direction, and circuit conditions to determine current.

reading.title: Two ways to rotate a sensor coil
reading.summary: An original experiment links orientation to changing flux.
body: A laboratory sensor uses a flat coil in a uniform, steady magnetic field. In trial A, the coil rotates so that the angle between its normal and the field changes from zero to ninety degrees. In trial B, the coil spins about its own normal while that normal remains parallel to the field. The number of turns, area and field magnitude are unchanged in both trials. A student expects equal induced emf because both coils are visibly rotating. The partner instead calculates flux from orientation. The coil terminals are connected only to an ideal voltmeter, so the experiment compares emf without assuming an appreciable current through a closed load.

questions.prompt: Which trial has a net change in flux from beginning to end?
options: Trial B only
Both trials have identical flux changes
Neither trial can change flux in a steady field
Trial A only
questions.hint: The field can remain steady while the orientation of the area changes.
questions.explanation: In A, flux changes from BA to zero per turn. In B, the normal remains parallel to the field, so BA cos θ stays constant despite visible rotation.

questions.prompt: Why is visible rotation alone insufficient to infer induced emf?
options: All rotations necessarily change the magnetic field strength
A coil can have no area if it rotates
Only rotation that changes flux linkage contributes through Faraday’s law
An ideal voltmeter creates the magnetic field
questions.hint: Track the quantity in Faraday’s law rather than motion alone.
questions.explanation: Flux linkage depends on field, area and orientation. Motion that leaves all relevant factors unchanged need not produce an emf in this idealised setting.

practice.title: A coil in a uniformly changing field
practice.summary: Calculate flux linkage, emf and current direction with explicit assumptions.
body: A 120-turn coil has area 0.015 m² per turn and total resistance 6.0 Ω in a closed circuit. Its normal is parallel to a uniform field directed into the page. The field increases linearly from 0.20 T to 0.50 T in 0.10 s. Ignore self-inductance and all other emf sources. View the coil directly face-on. After the change, the field is held constant at 0.50 T.

questions.prompt: What is the change in flux linkage during the increase?
options: 0.0045 Wb-turn
0.54 Wb-turn
0.90 Wb-turn
5.4 Wb-turn
questions.hint: Multiply the flux change per turn by 120.
questions.explanation: Δ(NΦ) = 120 × 0.015 × (0.50 − 0.20) = 0.54 Wb-turn. The value 0.0045 Wb is the flux change for one turn only.

questions.prompt: What is the emf magnitude during the linear increase?
questions.hint: Divide the linkage change by 0.10 s.
questions.explanation: |emf| = 0.54/0.10 = 5.4 V. The field changes at a constant rate, so the emf is constant during that interval under the assumptions.

questions.prompt: What are the induced current magnitude and direction during the increase?
options: 0.90 A, clockwise as viewed
3.24 A, anticlockwise as viewed
0.90 A, anticlockwise as viewed
0.09 A, clockwise as viewed
questions.hint: Use I = emf/R and oppose the increasing field into the page.
questions.explanation: I = 5.4/6.0 = 0.90 A. The coil’s induced field must point out of the page to oppose the increase into the page; the right-hand rule gives anticlockwise current.

questions.prompt: What is the induced emf once the field is constant, under the stated assumptions?
options: 0 V
questions.hint: A nonzero flux is different from a changing flux.
questions.explanation: With area and orientation fixed and B constant, flux linkage no longer changes. Faraday’s law therefore gives zero induced emf, although the magnetic field remains nonzero.

note.title: Equilibrium composition and reaction quotient
note.summary: Predict the direction of change by comparing Qc with Kc.
body: For a reaction written with specified stoichiometric coefficients, the equilibrium constant relates equilibrium concentrations at a given temperature. The reaction quotient Qc uses the same expression with the current concentrations. If Qc is below Kc, the forward reaction is favoured until equilibrium is restored; if Qc is above Kc, the reverse direction is favoured.

Worked example: for N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), suppose equilibrium concentrations are [N₂O₄] = 0.040 mol dm⁻³ and [NO₂] = 0.120 mol dm⁻³. Then Kc = [NO₂]²/[N₂O₄] = 0.360 mol dm⁻³ in this concentration convention. The coefficient two becomes a power; it is not multiplied directly by concentration.

A common misconception says a catalyst increases the equilibrium yield. It accelerates approach to equilibrium without changing Kc at the same temperature. Changing temperature can change Kc. Changing volume can alter concentrations and Qc immediately, after which the mixture may react towards a new equilibrium composition.
keyPoints: Use equilibrium concentrations for Kc and current concentrations for Qc.
Stoichiometric coefficients become powers in the expression.
Separate changes in rate, composition and the equilibrium constant.

reading.title: A catalyst in a sealed reaction vessel
reading.summary: An original comparison distinguishes faster equilibration from a different equilibrium.
body: Two sealed vessels contain identical initial mixtures for the model reaction A(g) + B(g) ⇌ C(g). Both vessels are kept at the same constant temperature and volume. A suitable catalyst is added to one vessel. Measurements show that its concentrations become steady after four minutes, while the uncatalysed vessel requires twenty minutes. At the end, both vessels have [A] = 0.50 mol dm⁻³, [B] = 0.50 mol dm⁻³ and [C] = 1.00 mol dm⁻³. A student says the catalyst has made the reaction more product-favoured. The teacher asks the student to distinguish the time taken from the final concentration ratio before interpreting the results.

questions.prompt: What value of Kc is obtained from either final mixture?
options: 2.00 dm³ mol⁻¹
4.00 dm³ mol⁻¹
0.25 dm³ mol⁻¹
1.00 dm³ mol⁻¹
questions.hint: Use [C]/([A][B]) for the reaction as written.
questions.explanation: Kc = 1.00/(0.50 × 0.50) = 4.00 dm³ mol⁻¹ in the stated concentration convention. Both final mixtures give the same value.

questions.prompt: Which interpretation best matches the observations?
options: The catalyst quadruples Kc because four minutes were required
The uncatalysed vessel cannot ever reach equilibrium
The catalyst changes the reaction’s stoichiometric coefficients
The catalyst reduces the time to reach equilibrium without changing the final equilibrium ratio
questions.hint: Compare the measured final concentrations as well as the times.
questions.explanation: The mixtures reach identical final concentration ratios at the same temperature. The difference is kinetic: the catalysed system reaches that state sooner.

practice.title: Dimer dissociation under changed conditions
practice.summary: Combine mole-to-concentration conversion with equilibrium reasoning.
body: For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), a closed 2.00 dm³ vessel initially contains 1.00 mol N₂O₄ and no NO₂. At equilibrium at temperature T, 0.400 mol N₂O₄ remains. The forward dissociation is endothermic. Assume ideal gas behaviour and use concentration-based Kc. For the expansion case only, the equilibrium mixture is suddenly expanded to 4.00 dm³ at the same T; consider the instant before further reaction.

questions.prompt: How many moles of NO₂ are present at the original equilibrium?
options: 1.20 mol
2.00 mol
questions.hint: Each mole of N₂O₄ consumed produces two moles of NO₂.
questions.explanation: N₂O₄ consumed = 1.00 − 0.400 = 0.600 mol. Stoichiometry gives 2 × 0.600 = 1.20 mol NO₂.

questions.prompt: What is Kc at temperature T?
options: 3.60 mol dm⁻³
1.80 mol dm⁻³
0.900 mol dm⁻³
0.300 mol dm⁻³
questions.hint: Convert each equilibrium amount using the original 2.00 dm³ volume.
questions.explanation: [N₂O₄] = 0.200 and [NO₂] = 0.600 mol dm⁻³. Kc = 0.600²/0.200 = 1.80 mol dm⁻³; substituting mole amounts directly would give a different and incorrect value.

questions.prompt: Immediately after expansion, how does Qc compare with Kc and which direction follows?
options: Qc = 1.80 mol dm⁻³, so composition cannot change
Qc = 3.60 mol dm⁻³, so net reaction proceeds forward
Qc = 0.900 mol dm⁻³, so net reaction proceeds in reverse
Qc = 0.900 mol dm⁻³, so net reaction proceeds forward
questions.hint: Amounts initially stay fixed while concentrations halve.
questions.explanation: After expansion, [NO₂] = 0.300 and [N₂O₄] = 0.100. Qc = 0.300²/0.100 = 0.900 < 1.80, so further dissociation raises the quotient towards Kc.

questions.prompt: What happens to Kc if temperature is increased for this endothermic forward reaction?
options: Kc decreases
Kc is necessarily unchanged because volume is fixed
Kc increases
Kc becomes zero for every endothermic reaction
questions.hint: Use the supplied enthalpy direction, not the presence of a catalyst.
questions.explanation: Higher temperature favours the endothermic direction, increasing the equilibrium product-to-reactant ratio in the Kc expression. Unlike a catalyst, a temperature change can alter Kc.

note.title: Enzyme saturation and competitive inhibition
note.summary: Interpret rate data using a defined model and controlled conditions.
body: Enzyme reaction rates depend on substrate availability as well as enzyme concentration and conditions. In the Michaelis–Menten model, v = Vmax[S]/(Km + [S]). Vmax is the limiting rate at high substrate concentration, while Km equals the substrate concentration at half Vmax. These parameters describe a model fitted under specified conditions.

Worked example: let Vmax = 120 arbitrary rate units and Km = 3 mmol dm⁻³. At [S] = 3, v = 60. If a reversible competitive inhibitor raises the apparent Km to 9 while Vmax stays 120, the predicted rate at the same substrate concentration becomes 30. More substrate is needed to attain half the limiting rate.

A common misconception says every inhibitor lowers Vmax. In ideal competitive inhibition, sufficiently high substrate can approach the same limit. A matching rate pattern supports that model but does not by itself reveal an inhibitor’s complete molecular structure. Temperature, pH and enzyme amount must remain controlled for comparisons.
keyPoints: Km is the substrate concentration giving half Vmax in this model.
Ideal competitive inhibition raises apparent Km without lowering Vmax.
Control experimental conditions and distinguish model support from molecular proof.

reading.title: Two rate curves in a teaching laboratory
reading.summary: An original dataset requires a cautious mechanistic interpretation.
body: A teaching laboratory measures initial rates of the same enzyme with and without substance X. Temperature, pH and enzyme concentration are held constant. At low substrate concentrations, rates with X are smaller. As substrate concentration becomes very high, both curves approach 100 arbitrary rate units. The substrate concentration giving a rate of 50 units is 2 mmol dm⁻³ without X and 6 mmol dm⁻³ with X. The students propose an ideal competitive inhibition model. Their supervisor accepts it as a useful explanation of the pattern but asks for additional experiments before claiming the exact binding interaction of X has been directly observed.

questions.prompt: What parameter pattern is supported by the observations?
options: Lower Vmax with unchanged apparent Km
Both Vmax and apparent Km become zero
Unchanged Vmax with a larger apparent Km in the presence of X
Vmax triples while apparent Km is unchanged
questions.hint: Identify the common plateau and the concentration at half that plateau.
questions.explanation: Both curves approach 100, so Vmax is unchanged in the fitted model. Half-maximal rate requires 6 rather than 2 mmol dm⁻³ substrate with X, indicating a larger apparent Km.

questions.prompt: Why is the supervisor’s qualification appropriate?
options: A rate pattern can support a mechanism without directly observing its molecular binding details
All enzyme rate measurements are meaningless
Matching Vmax proves that X has no effect at any substrate concentration
The experiment demonstrates that temperature was uncontrolled
questions.hint: Separate an inferred model from a directly measured molecular event.
questions.explanation: The observations are consistent with competitive inhibition under the stated assumptions. They do not directly image binding or uniquely establish every molecular detail.

practice.title: Calculate rates and test an enzyme model
practice.summary: Use the supplied equation to compare substrate and enzyme changes.
body: Use v = Vmax[S]/(Km + [S]). Without inhibitor, Vmax = 80 μmol min⁻¹ and Km = 4 mmol dm⁻³. With an ideal reversible competitive inhibitor, Vmax remains 80 μmol min⁻¹ and apparent Km becomes 12 mmol dm⁻³. Temperature, pH and the original enzyme amount are fixed unless a question explicitly changes them. Initial rates are measured before substantial substrate depletion.

questions.prompt: What is the uninhibited rate at [S] = 4 mmol dm⁻³?
options: 80 μmol min⁻¹
20 μmol min⁻¹
10 μmol min⁻¹
40 μmol min⁻¹
questions.hint: At substrate concentration equal to Km, the rate is half Vmax.
questions.explanation: v = 80 × 4/(4 + 4) = 40 μmol min⁻¹. Substrate equal to Km does not produce the full limiting rate.

questions.prompt: What is the inhibited rate at the same [S] = 4 mmol dm⁻³?
options: 40 μmol min⁻¹
20 μmol min⁻¹
60 μmol min⁻¹
80 μmol min⁻¹
questions.hint: Use the apparent Km of 12 for the inhibited model.
questions.explanation: v = 80 × 4/(12 + 4) = 20 μmol min⁻¹. The limiting rate is unchanged, but this substrate level is insufficient to approach it.

questions.prompt: What substrate concentration gives an inhibited rate of 40 μmol min⁻¹?
options: 4 mmol dm⁻³
8 mmol dm⁻³
12 mmol dm⁻³
24 mmol dm⁻³
questions.hint: Forty is half the inhibited Vmax.
questions.explanation: 40 = 80S/(12 + S) gives 480 + 40S = 80S, hence S = 12 mmol dm⁻³. This is the apparent Km for the inhibited condition.

questions.prompt: If enzyme amount is doubled without inhibitor, what does the ideal model predict at [S] = 4 mmol dm⁻³?
options: Km doubles to 8 while Vmax remains 80
Vmax doubles to 160 and the rate becomes 80 μmol min⁻¹
Vmax remains 80 and the rate must remain 40
The rate becomes zero because enzyme is in excess
questions.hint: In the ideal model, more active enzyme increases capacity while Km remains fixed.
questions.explanation: Doubling active enzyme doubles Vmax, with Km still 4. The predicted rate is 160 × 4/(4 + 4) = 80 μmol min⁻¹, assuming the stated initial-rate conditions remain valid.

note.title: Momen daya dalam model biomekanik
note.summary: Menghubungkan daya, jarak serenjang dan keseimbangan putaran.
body: Analisis biomekanik boleh memodelkan anggota sebagai segmen tegar yang berputar pada sendi. Momen daya bergantung pada magnitud daya serta jarak serenjang dari paksi kepada garis tindakannya: τ = Fd. Untuk keadaan statik, jumlah momen mengikut jam dan melawan jam seimbang; keseimbangan daya juga perlu dipenuhi jika semua daya hendak ditentukan.

Contoh kerja: beban 40 N bertindak pada jarak serenjang 0.30 m dari siku, menghasilkan momen 12 N m. Jika daya otot mempunyai lengan momen 0.040 m dan tiada momen lain dalam model, daya otot yang menyeimbangkan beban ialah 12/0.040 = 300 N. Lengan momen kecil boleh memerlukan daya dalaman yang jauh lebih besar daripada beban luar.

Salah tanggapan ialah menggunakan panjang anggota terus sebagai lengan momen bagi semua daya. Sudut garis tindakan menentukan jarak serenjang sebenar. Model ringkas berguna untuk menjelaskan prinsip, tetapi bentuk sendi, beberapa otot dan gerakan dinamik mengehadkan penggunaannya bagi tubuh sebenar.
keyPoints: Lengan momen ialah jarak serenjang kepada garis tindakan daya.
Imbangi semua momen yang diberikan sekitar paksi yang sama.
Nyatakan andaian model sebelum mentafsir daya dalaman.

reading.title: Dua kedudukan beban dalam demonstrasi
reading.summary: Kes pengajaran asli tentang mengapa beban sama boleh terasa berbeza.
body: Dalam demonstrasi biomekanik menggunakan model lengan, daya beban yang sama diletakkan pada dua kedudukan. Pada kedudukan A, jarak serenjang dari paksi siku ialah 0.25 m; pada B, jaraknya 0.15 m. Berat segmen dan lengan momen daya otot dikekalkan dalam model. Seorang pelajar menjangka daya otot sama kerana beban luar tidak berubah. Pelajar lain membezakan magnitud daya daripada kesan putarannya. Pensyarah meminta mereka mengira momen beban dahulu dan menyatakan andaian sebelum membincangkan daya otot. Demonstrasi ini ialah analisis model statik, bukan arahan memilih beban senaman atau kaedah merawat kecederaan.

questions.prompt: Bagaimanakah momen beban pada B dibandingkan dengan A?
options: Momen B ialah 60% daripada momen A
Momen B ialah 40% daripada momen A
Momen B ialah 150% daripada momen A
Kedua-dua momen semestinya sama
questions.hint: Daya sama, jadi nisbah momen sama dengan nisbah jarak serenjang.
questions.explanation: τB/τA = 0.15/0.25 = 0.60. Magnitud beban sahaja tidak menentukan momen; kedudukan garis tindakannya turut penting.

questions.prompt: Jika momen berat segmen dan lengan momen otot kekal, apakah kesan memindahkan beban dari A ke B?
options: Daya otot mesti menjadi sifar
Daya otot pasti meningkat kerana jarak berkurang
Berat segmen berubah menjadi sifar
Daya otot untuk keseimbangan statik menjadi lebih kecil
questions.hint: Jumlah momen luar berkurang sementara pembahagi bagi daya otot kekal.
questions.explanation: Momen beban berkurang, jadi jumlah momen yang perlu diimbangi otot juga berkurang. Momen berat segmen masih ada, maka daya tidak semestinya sifar.

practice.title: Keseimbangan momen pada segmen lengan
practice.summary: Menyelesaikan model statik dengan dua daya luar dan satu daya otot.
body: Model lengan bawah mendatar berpaksi pada siku. Beban 60 N bertindak ke bawah pada jarak 0.30 m dari siku. Berat segmen 20 N bertindak ke bawah pada jarak 0.15 m. Daya otot menghasilkan momen bertentangan dengan lengan momen serenjang 0.035 m. Abaikan momen lain. Daya tindak balas sendi melalui paksi dan tidak menghasilkan momen tentang paksi itu. Untuk kes pemindahan beban sahaja, beban 60 N dipindahkan ke jarak 0.20 m.

questions.prompt: Berapakah jumlah momen kedua-dua daya ke bawah dalam keadaan asal?
options: 18 N m
21 N m
3 N m
24 N m
questions.hint: Jumlahkan momen beban dan berat segmen tentang siku.
questions.explanation: Momen beban = 60 × 0.30 = 18 N m; momen segmen = 20 × 0.15 = 3 N m. Kedua-duanya searah, jadi jumlahnya 21 N m.

questions.prompt: Berapakah daya otot untuk keseimbangan momen asal?
questions.hint: Daya otot didarab lengan momennya mesti menghasilkan 21 N m.
questions.explanation: F × 0.035 = 21, maka F = 600 N. Daya dalaman besar berpunca daripada lengan momen otot yang pendek dalam model ini.

questions.prompt: Selepas beban dipindahkan ke 0.20 m, berapakah daya otot baharu, dibundarkan kepada tiga angka bererti?
questions.hint: Kira semula momen beban tetapi kekalkan momen berat segmen.
questions.explanation: Momen baharu = 60(0.20) + 20(0.15) = 15 N m. F = 15/0.035 = 428.571… N, iaitu 429 N; mengabaikan berat segmen akan memberi nilai terlalu kecil.

questions.prompt: Mengapakah model ini tidak menentukan daya sendi sepenuhnya melalui persamaan momen sahaja?
options: Semua daya yang tiada momen mesti mempunyai magnitud sifar
Sendi tidak pernah mengalami sebarang daya
Daya sendi melalui paksi, jadi momennya sifar walaupun magnitud dayanya belum diketahui
Keseimbangan momen secara automatik memberikan semua komponen daya
questions.hint: Bezakan persamaan keseimbangan putaran daripada keseimbangan translasi.
questions.explanation: Daya melalui paksi tidak muncul dalam jumlah momen tentang paksi itu. Komponen arah dan keseimbangan daya diperlukan untuk menentukan tindak balas sendi, dan arah penuh daya otot belum diberikan.

note.title: Analisis formal dan hierarki makna
note.summary: Menghubungkan susunan visual dengan tafsiran dan tujuan komunikasi.
body: Analisis formal meneliti hubungan unsur seperti garisan, rupa, warna, jalinan dan ruang dengan prinsip penyusunan. Penegasan boleh terhasil melalui kontras saiz, tona atau kedudukan. Keseimbangan tidak semestinya simetri: bentuk kecil yang sangat berbeza boleh mengimbangi perhatian terhadap bentuk lebih besar. Tafsiran perlu menjelaskan cara mata diarahkan dan kaitannya dengan tujuan karya.

Contoh kerja: poster rekaan memaparkan satu bekas air biru kecil di tengah latar kelabu luas, dengan angka besar tentang penggunaan air di bahagian atas. Kontras warna menarik perhatian pada bekas, sementara saiz angka menetapkan hierarki maklumat. Jika butiran tindakan terlalu kecil, poster mungkin menarik perhatian tetapi gagal membantu khalayak bertindak.

Salah tanggapan ialah menganggap warna mempunyai satu makna universal yang pasti. Konteks, hubungan visual dan pengalaman khalayak mempengaruhi tafsiran. Penilaian yang kukuh memisahkan pemerhatian bentuk daripada tafsiran makna, kemudian menguji sama ada pilihan visual menyokong mesej dan kebolehbacaan.
keyPoints: Hubungkan setiap istilah formal dengan bukti visual yang khusus.
Bezakan penegasan, keseimbangan dan hierarki maklumat.
Uji tafsiran warna serta simbol melalui konteks, bukan andaian universal.

reading.title: Poster “Ruang Untuk Semua” rekaan
reading.summary: Senario visual asli tentang perhatian dan kebolehcapaian maklumat.
body: Sebuah poster rekaan bagi pameran komuniti menggunakan latar putih dan tajuk hitam besar. Di sebelah kiri terdapat enam bentuk manusia kelabu yang rapat; di sebelah kanan, satu bentuk merah dipisahkan oleh ruang kosong luas. Tarikh dan lokasi dicetak dalam kelabu sangat pucat pada bahagian bawah. Pereka menyatakan bahawa bentuk merah menimbulkan persoalan tentang keterasingan. Seorang pengulas bersetuju bahawa kontras warna dan jarak boleh menyokong tafsiran itu, tetapi mengingatkan bahawa penonton belum tentu mengenal pasti maksud yang sama. Dalam ujian ringkas, ramai peserta melihat bentuk merah dahulu tetapi beberapa orang gagal membaca lokasi pameran dari jarak biasa.

questions.prompt: Apakah bukti formal paling langsung yang menyokong tafsiran keterasingan?
options: Tajuk menggunakan huruf yang boleh dibaca
Poster mempunyai bahagian atas dan bawah
Semua bentuk diberi warna dan jarak yang sama
Pemisahan ruang dan perbezaan warna satu bentuk daripada kelompok
questions.hint: Gabungkan hubungan ruang dengan kontras pada bentuk tunggal.
questions.explanation: Bentuk merah berbeza dan terpisah daripada kelompok kelabu. Gabungan itu menyokong tafsiran sosial, walaupun tidak memaksa semua penonton memberikan makna yang sama.

questions.prompt: Apakah pindaan paling langsung menangani dapatan ujian lokasi?
options: Tambahkan lebih banyak bentuk merah tanpa mengubah teks
Padamkan lokasi untuk meluaskan tafsiran
Tingkatkan kontras tona dan kebolehbacaan maklumat lokasi
Kekalkan teks pucat kerana perhatian pertama sudah berjaya
questions.hint: Masalah yang diperhatikan ialah pembacaan maklumat tindakan.
questions.explanation: Kontras teks terhadap latar perlu cukup untuk dibaca. Penegasan imej dan kejelasan maklumat ialah fungsi berbeza yang kedua-duanya penting bagi poster acara.

practice.title: Membandingkan dua susun atur pameran
practice.summary: Menilai pilihan reka bentuk melalui pemerhatian dan tujuan.
body: Dua poster rekaan mempromosikan bengkel seni yang sama. Versi A memberi saiz sama kepada tajuk, huraian 180 patah perkataan, tarikh, lokasi dan pautan pendaftaran; semua teks disusun rapat. Versi B menggunakan tajuk besar, ringkasan 25 patah perkataan, tarikh dan lokasi sederhana besar serta pautan pendaftaran yang dipisahkan oleh ruang. Kedua-duanya menggunakan warna yang sama. Matlamat ialah membantu pembaca mengenal pasti acara dan cara mendaftar dengan cepat, sambil mengekalkan maklumat penting.

questions.prompt: Apakah perbezaan formal utama yang paling berkaitan dengan matlamat?
options: B menggunakan warna yang sama, maka tiada perbezaan boleh wujud
B membentuk hierarki melalui perbezaan saiz, panjang teks dan ruang
A pasti lebih jelas kerana semua perkara bersaiz sama
A menghapuskan semua huraian acara
questions.hint: Fokus pada susunan maklumat, bukan warna sahaja.
questions.explanation: B membezakan tahap kepentingan dan mengasingkan tindakan pendaftaran. Hierarki boleh dibentuk melalui beberapa pemboleh ubah walaupun palet warna tidak berubah.

questions.prompt: Apakah fungsi ruang di sekitar pautan pendaftaran dalam B?
options: Mengasingkan tindakan utama supaya lebih mudah dikenal pasti
Membuktikan pereka terlupa menambah kandungan
Menjadikan setiap pembaca pasti mendaftar
Menghapuskan keperluan pautan yang berfungsi
questions.hint: Nilai ruang sebagai sebahagian hubungan antara unsur.
questions.explanation: Ruang membantu membezakan pautan daripada maklumat lain dan boleh meningkatkan kebolehlihatan. Ia tidak menjamin tindakan atau menggantikan fungsi pautan.

questions.prompt: Ujian manakah paling sepadan dengan tujuan yang dinyatakan?
options: Tanya warna kegemaran pereka sahaja
Kira jumlah piksel tanpa melihat tugasan pembaca
Minta khalayak sasaran mencari tarikh, lokasi dan cara mendaftar; rekod ketepatan serta masa
Pilih poster berdasarkan saiz fail terbesar
questions.hint: Ukuran harus menguji tugas komunikasi sebenar.
questions.explanation: Ketepatan dan masa mencari maklumat mengukur kejelasan praktikal yang menjadi matlamat. Keutamaan pereka atau saiz fail tidak mengukur kejayaan tugas itu secara langsung.

questions.prompt: Apakah batas yang perlu diperiksa apabila huraian dipendekkan daripada 180 kepada 25 perkataan?
options: Pastikan syarat penting penyertaan tidak hilang walaupun bacaan menjadi cepat
Semua ayat panjang semestinya tidak mempunyai makna
Ringkasan menjamin tiada maklumat boleh tertinggal
Maklumat lokasi perlu dibuang untuk mengekalkan ruang
questions.hint: Kecekapan membaca perlu diseimbangkan dengan kelengkapan maklumat penting.
questions.explanation: Pemendekan boleh membantu tumpuan tetapi mungkin menggugurkan kelayakan, bahan diperlukan atau syarat lain. Semakan kandungan memastikan hierarki yang jelas masih menyampaikan perkara yang diperlukan pembaca.
